introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Citizenship Education 2 (0562), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2019. Duration: Two and a half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

- You are required to answer FOUR questions choosing QUESTION 1 and THREE others from Sections A, B, and C.
- All the questions carry equal marks and marks allocated to different parts of questions are indicated.
- Extra question(s) answered from each section shall NOT be marked.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**Question 1**

Study this extract bearing on the Natural Environment of a Community and then answer questions (a) to (e) that follow. (The maximum marks for each sub-question is indicated in brackets)

> Human and natural activities are the principal causes of environmental degradation.
>
> Some natural factors of environmental degradation includes: Acid rain, volcanic eruptions, excess rain fall and floods. Etc
>
> On the other hand, we also have human factors such as pollution, the use of fossil fuels, deforestation and rapid urbanisation. These natural and human factors have produced detrimental effects on the environment in recent times. This situation has brought in health difficulties, extreme weather conditions and loss of biodiversity.
>
> It is very certain and a regular phenomenon that human beings and nature all contribute to the negative and positive developments that take place in the environment today. Conservation practices have been put in place to improve on the damaging effects of our environment. The Government of Cameroon does so through the Ministry of Environment and Nature Protection. Some International Organisations and Non-Governmental Organisations also have been making efforts in regulating and prohibiting certain practices by man and nature. This will eventually render our environment a better place for human existence and build a save and decent society for all.

Source: Improvised.

Passage de la Question 1 recopié tel qu'imprimé, y compris ses fautes (« includes », « save and decent society », « Etc »). Le scan est de mauvaise qualité mais le texte est lisible.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Define Environmental Degradation.

(ii) Give TWO ways in which the environment is important to man.

(iii) Identify TWO forms of environmental degradation linked to man's activities as mentioned in the text.

(1 + 2 + 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Definition [1 mark].** Environmental degradation is the **deterioration or destruction of the natural environment** (air, water, soil, forests, wildlife) through the wearing out of natural resources and the damage done to ecosystems, either by natural events or, most often, by human activities.

**(ii) Two ways in which the environment is important to man [2 marks: 1 mark each].**

1. It **provides the basic needs of life**: air to breathe, water to drink, soil on which food is grown, and wood and stone for building shelter.
2. It **supplies raw materials and income**: timber, minerals, fish and farm products are used by industries and sold, giving jobs and money to people and to the State.

(Other acceptable points: the environment gives medicinal plants; it regulates the climate and rainfall; it offers places for tourism and recreation.)

**(iii) Two forms of environmental degradation linked to man's activities, as mentioned in the text [2 marks: 1 mark each].** The passage names the following human factors: **pollution, the use of fossil fuels, deforestation and rapid urbanisation.** Any two of these are correct, for example:

1. **Deforestation** - the cutting down of forests for timber, farmland, fuel wood and roads.
2. **Pollution** - the release of harmful waste into the air, water and soil.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Apart from the reasons listed in the text, give other causes of environmental degradation.

(ii) Identify and explain some other forms of pollution in Cameroon.

(2 + 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Other causes of environmental degradation [2 marks].** The text lists acid rain, volcanic eruptions, heavy rainfall and floods (natural causes) and pollution, the use of fossil fuels, deforestation and rapid urbanisation (human causes). Other causes include:

- **Bush burning and slash-and-burn farming**, which destroy vegetation and the organisms in the soil.
- **Overgrazing and overcultivation**, which leave the soil bare and exhausted, leading to erosion.
- **Mining, quarrying and sand extraction**, which leave open pits and destroy the land.
- **Overpopulation**, which increases the demand for land, food, water and fuel.
- **Poaching, overfishing and the over-exploitation of resources.**
- **Poor waste disposal and the use of chemicals** (pesticides, fertilisers) on farms.
- **Natural causes not listed in the passage**, such as drought, landslides and earthquakes.

**(ii) Other forms of pollution in Cameroon [2 marks].** The passage only mentions pollution in general. Some forms of pollution that are found in Cameroon:

- **Air pollution:** smoke from badly maintained vehicles, factories and the burning of rubbish and bush, which makes the air unhealthy to breathe.
- **Water pollution:** the dumping of household waste, plastic and industrial or farm chemicals in streams, rivers and the sea, which makes the water unsafe for drinking and kills fish.
- **Noise pollution:** loud music in bars, noisy motorbikes, generators and loudspeakers, which disturb rest and study and can damage hearing.
- **Land (soil) pollution:** plastic bags, waste and chemicals left on the ground, which reduce the fertility of the soil and block drains.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) What do you understand by conservation as mentioned in the passage?

(ii) Explain any practice carried out in your area to protect the environment.

(iii) Outline two major effects of environmental degradation on your community.

(1 + 1 + 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Conservation [1 mark].** In the passage, conservation means the **practices put in place to protect, preserve and wisely manage the environment and its resources** so as to improve on the damage done to the environment and to keep it useful for present and future generations.

**(ii) A practice carried out to protect the environment [1 mark].** A candidate may describe a practice that he or she knows in the community. Example: **tree planting (reforestation).** Pupils, villagers and councils plant trees along roads, around schools and on bare or eroded land. The trees hold the soil together and prevent erosion, give shade, absorb carbon dioxide, protect water sources and provide fruit and fuel wood. (Other acceptable practices: regular community clean-up and sanitation days, proper disposal of waste, digging pits and bins for rubbish, and the protection of water catchments.)

**(iii) Two major effects of environmental degradation on a community [2 marks: 1 mark each].**

1. **Health problems:** polluted air and dirty water cause respiratory diseases, cholera, typhoid, diarrhoea and malaria.
2. **Floods, erosion and loss of farmland:** when vegetation is removed, the soil is washed away, crops are destroyed and families lose their food and income.

(Other acceptable effects: shortage of drinking water, extreme weather conditions, loss of biodiversity, loss of homes.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Enumerate TWO effects of environmental degradation in your community.

(ii) Name one Ministry in Cameroon apart from the one mentioned in the passage that also protects the environment.

(2 + 1 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two effects of environmental degradation in a community [2 marks: 1 mark each].** For example:

1. **Loss of biodiversity:** animals and plants lose their habitats and some species become rare or disappear.
2. **Reduced harvests and poverty:** soil erosion, drought and floods reduce crop yields, so farmers earn less.

(Other acceptable effects: diseases, scarcity of clean water, extreme weather such as heavy rain or heat, displacement of families, higher cost of living.)

**(ii) Another Ministry that protects the environment [1 mark].** The passage mentions the Ministry of Environment and Nature Protection. Another ministry that protects the environment is the **Ministry of Forestry and Wildlife**, which manages forests and wildlife, fights illegal logging and poaching and looks after national parks and reserves.

(Other acceptable answers: the Ministry in charge of Water Resources and Energy, the Ministry of Urban Development and Housing, the Ministry of Public Health, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e) What role has the Government of Cameroon and N.G.Os played in the protection of the environment in recent times?

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The protection of the environment is a shared responsibility. In recent times the Government of Cameroon and Non-Governmental Organisations (N.G.Os) have both taken action.

**Role of the Government [2 marks].**

- It has set up a **ministry in charge of the environment and nature protection** (together with other ministries such as the one in charge of forestry and wildlife) to define and apply the national environmental policy.
- It has made **laws and regulations** on the management of the environment, forests, wildlife and waste, and requires environmental impact studies before major projects.
- It has created **protected areas** such as national parks, forest reserves and wildlife sanctuaries.
- It carries out **tree-planting and reforestation campaigns** and sensitisation campaigns (for example on World Environment Day).
- It has signed and ratified **international agreements** on the protection of the environment and the climate, and cooperates with international organisations.
- Councils are in charge of **sanitation and the collection of household waste** in their areas.

**Role of N.G.Os [2 marks].**

- They **educate and sensitise** the population on environmental protection, hygiene and climate change.
- They **organise tree planting, clean-up campaigns** and the protection of rivers and forests.
- They **protect wildlife and help local people** to farm in ways that do not destroy the forest (for example organisations such as WWF working in the forests of the country).
- They **provide funds, training and equipment**, do research, and put pressure on the government and companies to respect environmental rules.

**Conclusion.** Through laws, institutions, campaigns and projects, the Government and N.G.Os, helped by international organisations, are working to make the environment a better and safer place for everybody.
